justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I assumed was a current level near 1,085–1,087, with each successive horizon incorporating a small positive trend. For the one-day estimate, I leaned heavily on short-term momentum and mean-reversion tendencies, assuming no major overnight catalysts would dramatically reprice the asset. The one-week estimate nudges slightly higher to 1,092, reflecting a gentle continuation of whatever underlying trend was present, while acknowledging that weekly noise tends to dominate short-run signals. The one-month estimate of 1,100 extrapolates that same modest drift further, essentially assuming a slow grind higher consistent with a low-volatility, trending environment. In all three cases, I was not incorporating any strong directional conviction — these are near-baseline projections anchored close to the starting value.

The confidence interval widths widen progressively across horizons in a way that reflects standard volatility scaling — roughly proportional to the square root of time. At one day, the 90% interval spans about 64 units, which implies relatively tight intraday conditions. By one week that expands to 125 units, and by one month it reaches 240 units, reflecting the compounding uncertainty of news flow, macro data releases, and market sentiment shifts that accumulate over longer windows. The width of these intervals was also influenced by my assumption of moderate baseline volatility rather than an elevated or suppressed regime — had I believed we were in a high-volatility environment, the bands would be considerably wider.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes well outside my stated intervals. On the upside, a surprise positive catalyst — such as a significant policy announcement, strong economic data, or a short-squeeze dynamic — could push prices beyond the upper bound of even the one-month interval fairly quickly. On the downside, a risk-off episode triggered by geopolitical escalation, a financial stress event, or a sharp revision in central bank expectations could easily breach the lower bounds. Liquidity conditions also matter: thin markets can amplify moves in either direction, particularly around major data releases or end-of-month rebalancing flows. My intervals should be treated as reflecting a modal, relatively calm scenario rather than a guarantee of containment under stressed conditions.
